title: ആട് ജീവിതം Goat vs Sheep Explained | Science , Domestication & Culture ചെമ്മരിയാട് കോലാട് വ്യത്യാസം
description:
മനുഷ്യൻ ആദ്യമായി ഇണക്കി വളർത്താൻ തുടങ്ങിയ മൃഗങ്ങളിലൊന്നാണ് ആട്. എന്നാൽ ആടുകളെക്കുറിച്ച് നമുക്ക് അറിയാത്ത എത്രയോ ശാസ്ത്രീയ വശങ്ങളുണ്ട്! കോലാടുകളും (Goat) ചെമ്മരിയാടുകളും (Sheep) തമ്മിലുള്ള ജനിതക വ്യത്യാസങ്ങൾ എന്തൊക്കെയാണ്? അവ എങ്ങനെയാണ് പർവ്വതങ്ങളിൽ നിന്ന് നമ്മുടെ തൊഴുത്തുകളിലേക്ക് എത്തിയത്? വിവിധ മതങ്ങളിലും സംസ്‌കാരങ്ങളിലും ആടുകൾക്ക് ലഭിച്ച സ്ഥാനം എന്താണ്?
What’s the real difference between sheep and goats? 
In this video, we explore the complete scientific comparison between these two important domesticated animals.
✔️ Physical differences (horns, tail, body structure)
✔️ Behavioral differences (grazing vs browsing)
✔️ Scientific classification and evolution
✔️ Domestication history and origin
✔️ Importance in agriculture and economy
✔️ Cultural and religious significance across the world

Sheep and goats have been part of human civilization for thousands of years. From ancient farming societies to modern agriculture, they play a vital role in food, clothing, and culture.

A sheep with curly white fur, not leaving the flock, and a goat that was waiting to taste blood, biting each other with its horns. The first is a sheep in English, and the second is a goat, which we call a goat. Although the two are related, they are two different species. They are different creatures with different chromosome numbers. Goats have 60 chromosomes, while sheep have only 54 chromosomes. They do not even naturally interbreed to produce offspring. However, we call them both goats. These two types of goats are in the Caprine subfamily of the Bovid family, which includes cows, buffaloes, and antelopes. Get involved. However, a sheep-goat hybrid called a Geep is also produced through artificial insemination. But geeps are usually sterile. That means they will not have the ability to propagate. However, there have been some reported cases in New Zealand and France where geeps have mated and produced offspring, although it is not common. As you know, the first animal created by humans was the dog. Sheep are the ones we domesticated for milk, meat, and fur. We do not have complete knowledge about when and where humans first domesticated sheep. It is believed that the domestication of sheep occurred around the same time. It is believed that it began in the Fertile Crescent region of Western Asia during the Neolithic period, approximately 11,000 years ago. The earliest evidence of this has been found in the Zagros Mountains of Iran and Anatolia in Turkey. It is believed that our sheep and goats were domesticated by taming the wild sheep called the Asiatic mouflon, whose scientific name is Ovis gamlini. We first started killing them for their meat, milk, and leather. It is believed that they began to be raised for their fur late in life. The evidence for this comes later from Iran. Humans have been using their fur since at least 6000 BC . However, it was only two or three thousand years later that humans began to make woolen cloth from wool. In any case, widespread sheep farming began in Europe. In ancient Greece, people raised goats in large herds. With colonization, European sheep farming spread to the newly discovered New World after the 1490s . Our goats, which we call goats, were domesticated by the Bezoar Ibex, a wild goat that was once abundant in the mountainous regions of Anatolia in western Asia, including present-day Iran, northern Iraq, and southeastern Turkey. This happened about ten thousand years ago, during the domestication of sheep. It happened not in one place but in many places at various times. That is, at various times, different tribes selected and mated animals according to their different preferences and created various people. They considered their size, obedience, reproductive ability, coat color, length, shape, preferences for those with and without horns, and the size of the udder. They mated and tamed the goats and created new breeds. For example, the ancient Egyptians were more interested in goats with broken ears, hanging ears, and no horns. They were interested in raising them. Although humans began raising goats for their meat and milk, Starting from hunting, humans trained them to breed them in large numbers in cages, and to breed the best ones to create the type of sheep they needed. As part of domestication, changes occurred in their physical size and brain structure, and their ability to communicate with humans increased. Humans began to burn sheep dung and use their fur, bones, and tendons for various purposes. Goat skin containers were used to store and transport water and wine during travel. When the wine was sold, these goat skin containers were used to store and sell wine. In addition, various types of writing and documents were used to transfer and store them. It is estimated that goats reached the Nile River basin in Egypt about 7,000 years ago. From there, they slowly reached many places in Africa. The scientific name for goats is now Capra hircus, and for sheep, Ovis aries. There are very large breeds of goats, weighing up to 140 kilograms. Sometimes the South African meat goat, the Boer or Boerbak, can be close to a meter tall. However, no matter how big they are, there is a limit to how much goats can grow. Goats are animals with a milk-producing nature, so they have many characteristics of other animals that produce milk. The udder of goats is made up of different mammary glands. Each gland has a nipple. Cows have four nipples, while goats have only two nipples. However, Boer goats sometimes have up to eight nipples. There is a gap that separates the two halves of the udder, which is called the intermammary groove. Goats usually reach puberty in seven to 12 months, but for healthy breeding, it is always better for ewes to have 9 to 10 months. The menstrual cycle of ewes The estrus cycle lasts from 18 to 21 days, and lasts from 12 to 36 hours. This period of heat is called the heat duration. During this period, they will show symptoms such as excessive tail wagging, frequent urination, decreased feed intake, and swelling of the genitals. They also have an odor produced by the glands attached to the horns on the head of the ewes. Pheromones such as phoritha octanol are the main components of this odor. This odor triggers ovulation, stimulates the uterus, and helps in expressing the mating signals. The gestation period of the sheep is 150 days. About five months before the birth, the udder swells and the sheep shows discomfort. Our Malabari sheep are very famous for their high reproductive capacity. 50% of these births have twins and 25% have triplets, but in Attappadi Black sheep, usually only one child is born. According to Guinness World Records, the largest number of lambs born in a single birth was a Nigerian dwarf goat, with seven babies. Most goat breeds have a lifespan of 14 to 20 years . However, the nutrition, climate, and health care provided to sheep all influence their lifespan . The most interesting thing is that our goats and our regular sheep have tails that stand up. Meanwhile, the sheep's tail is downwards . Our goats sometimes have beards, both male and female, and the length varies depending on the breed, and some do not. However, sheep do not have such a special beard for males and females. In addition to this, our common sheep, which are also called goats, have a finger-like organ on both sides of the neck, which is a reason for calling them wattled goats. This is scientifically called the appendix colli or wattles . These are cartilages made of skin. It contains blood vessels, nerves, and muscles. Currently, no specific physical characteristics have been identified for them. It is now thought that these horns may be some vestigial organ left over from the evolutionary process, or they may be the remains of evolved limbs. One thing that is passed down from generation to generation is the dominant inheritance. A cleft philtrum can be seen in the middle of the upper lip of sheep, which goats do not have. Their horns are also unique. Our goats have horns that are usually flat towards the mouth and curved backwards, but sheep's horns are spirally curled. However, in general, both males and females of sheep breeds often do not have horns. Sometimes there are breeds where only the female has no horns. However, among goat breeds, there are very few breeds that do not have horns. Usually, these goats have a pair of horns, but rarely, there are goats with four or eight horns. If there are goats with no horns at all, then Attempts to create breeds are not very successful because the sex- determining gene and the horn gene are linked, meaning that offspring produced by mating hornless sheep will have some problems with their sex, and will often be infertile. The horns of sheep are made of living bones, surrounded by a covering of keratin and other proteins. People use these horns for defense, dominance, and territory protection. These horns also help them to regulate their temperature to a small extent. Now, when it comes to hair, sheep have very curly, wiry hair. They have wool. While special breeds such as the Agora Kashmiri, goats usually have long hair. Their color also varies depending on the breed. Their ancestors, who were used for domestication, had hair in the wild days that was brown or in different shades of brown. There used to be, but through selective breeding, there are now sheep with pearly white hair, ranging from chocolate brown to dark brown. Rarely, there are sheep with spots and sometimes spots. Since white hair is easy to dye and the white hair gene is a dominant trait, such babies are more common. Kashmiri sheep are found in areas such as the Himalayan mountains, where there is severe cold. In addition to the outer hard hair called guard hairs to protect them from the extreme cold, there is also a dead and thin undercoat underneath. This is what is collected for Kashmiri wool. The best type of Kashmiri wool is Pashmina. It is collected from Chang Tangya sheep, which grows only in the highlands of Ladakh and Kashmir. Pashmina, the deadest hair in the world, is hand-woven. Shawls are very expensive because they are not sheared like regular sheep, but are combed and separated with a comb when they shed their hair in the spring. These cashmere fibers help provide three times the warmth of regular hair. Their diameter is less than 19 microns. Similarly, mohair is obtained from Angora goats in Turkey. Their hair is long, shiny, and silky. The way sheep forage is also different. Our goats are browsers, meaning they choose and eat leaves, shoots, and thorns of plants, but sheep are grazers, meaning they prefer to nibble on grass on the ground, even though they are important. Sheep have rectangular pupils that are rectangular in shape, which gives them a panoramic view of 320 to 340 degrees, meaning they can see almost everything around them without turning their heads. The most interesting thing is that when goats lower and raise their heads, their irises rotate inside their eyes to remain parallel to the ground. This is called cyclovergence. Also, like elephants, goats do not have tear glands. There is no tear duct. In some children's literature, the mother goat is seen passing her babies to someone else and shedding tears. Sometimes it doesn't matter. Goats don't have tears to cry. In any case, many studies have shown that sheep have incredible intelligence. They can learn complex tasks and remember them for up to 10 months. Goats are more capable than sheep of quickly understanding and remembering information. Goats have the ability to recognize human facial expressions. People like to interact more with people who have happy, smiling faces. In some parades, they are seen to preferentially choose smiling faces over angry ones. When they need help, they look at people's faces and communicate. Sheep always like to live in groups, are flock-oriented, and fearful. They have a dominance hierarchy. When a leader walks forward, they all move with them. They move together without leaving the group. Since they live in groups like this, they do not like to leave the group. It is believed that humans have domesticated them more and more. If you let them out into a meadow, goats will wander and graze in different places, while sheep will graze in groups. However, goats are excellent climbers. They can climb even rocks with an inclination of more than 60 degrees. Sheep in Morocco can climb up to 10 meters above argan trees and eat leaves. However, sheep do not have this ability. Sheep meat has seven times more fat and twice as many calories than goat meat. Goat meat has more iron, copper, potassium, etc. than sheep meat. When we ask small classes to perform mimicry, the first thing they train in schools is the cry of a sheep. After the voice of a crow, the cries of sheep are the easiest for us to imitate. But the cries of sheep are not all the same. It is believed that just as we humans have unique accents or styles from different regions, sheep also have these distinctive sounds . This means that there will be significant differences between the sounds of sheep raised in different flocks . Now, we call the sounds that sheep make as crying. They don't actually faint, but rather a genetic condition called myotonia congenita, which causes their muscles to suddenly stiffen and stiffen. Sheep don't just sneeze. A Nubian lamb named Simba from Pakistan holds the record for having the largest ears, with 19 inches long ears. These long ears help keep them cool in hot weather. Goats have a special place in human history and culture. The chariot of the Norse god Thor is pulled by two rams who hunt them for food. Even if they were killed, they could be brought back to life with Thor's magic hammer. According to ancient Sumerian belief, the god of water, MK, was the symbol of the god of water. This is the Capricorn that later became the Capricorn sign, which is used in our astrology and astronomy. Goats have a special place in Hindu religious beliefs and mythology. The vehicle of the god of fire is a ram. This symbolizes agility and the power to overcome certain obstacles. Very rarely, goats are depicted pulling the chariot of fire. And the ram is also considered the vehicle of Kubera, the god of wealth. An important event in Hindu mythology is the giving of a ram's head to Daksha Prajapati. The story goes that Daksha, who insulted Lord Shiva, was beheaded by Veerabhadra, and later, when he repented, he was given a ram's head as a symbol of abandoning his pride and accepting humility. Shiva revived him. Since ancient times, people in many parts of the world have sacrificed sheep as part of their beliefs and rituals. The goat has a special place in these rituals, which aim to please God and forgive sins. Sheep were widely sacrificed in ancient Egypt to ensure the fertility of the land and the abundance of the Nile River . The practice of sacrificing sheep for healing and to please the gods was prevalent in Sumerian and Babylonian cultures for a long time. The sacrifice, considered the most sacred among Muslims, takes place during Eid al-Adha. Believers believe that this ritual commemorates the unwavering faith of Prophet Ibrahim, who was willing to sacrifice his beloved son Ismail at God's command. It is believed that at that moment, Allah intervened and sacrificed a goat in place of his son . This type of goat sacrifice is also practiced in powerful rituals in Hinduism. There was a ritual of sacrificing black goats to appease the fierce deities, such as Kali, Durga, and Bhairava, and to ward off evil. Despite legal prohibitions, this type of goat sacrifice is still practiced in some villages in northern Kerala. Sometimes it is done symbolically as part of rituals, sometimes it is done only. Let's end this video by mentioning the scapegoat. A word we often hear is scapegoat. In sociology, the term scapegoat is used to describe an innocent person who is condemned to take the blame for the failures and crimes of a group or individual. In our language, the term scapegoat is used as a scapegoat in English. The term comes from Jewish customs described in the Old Testament of the Bible. Two goats are chosen during Yom Kippur, the Jewish Day of Atonement. One of them is offered as a sacrifice to God, and the priest lays his hands on the head of the second goat, confessing all the sins of the people and symbolically placing them on its head. This goat, burdened with sin, is then taken to a desolate wilderness with a specially appointed person and released. It is believed that through this, the sins of the people are washed away . In the Second Temple period, in order to prevent this sin from returning to humans, there was also a custom of throwing the goat off a mountaintop and killing it. In 1530, William Tyne, when translating the Bible, first used the term "escaping goat" to mean an escaping goat. He gave an interpretation of the Hebrew word "Azazel" as "goat" and "goda depart". According to Christian theology, Jesus Christ is considered the ultimate scapegoat who took the sins of the world on his shoulders and is the ultimate super god . Ancient Greece also had similar ceremonies and rituals. In times of calamities like drought or plague, criminals or the poor are deported or physically tortured as scapegoats to save society. Although legal restrictions have been introduced over time, in many places this poor animal is still sacrificed as part of local customs and beliefs.
